source: Vynatheya, Mardling and Hamers 2023, MNRAS 525, 3 (arXiv 2301.09930); weights from https://github.com/pavanvyn/quadruple-stability, mlp_model_3p1_ghost_v1.2.2.pkl (read 2026-10-30 without running its code, scripts/build_quadruple_stability.py)

stable_below.basis: classify_quad_3p1.py of the authors: a system is stable when the network's probability of 'unstable' is below 0.5

q_in_min.basis: paper section 3.1: masses log-uniform over one order of magnitude, so the inner mass ratio m2/m1 is at least 0.1

q_mid_max.basis: the help text of classify_quad_3p1.py: 'best if < ~3'; the paper's masses give m3/(m1+m2) up to 5 but the authors say to stay under about 3

q_out_max.basis: the help text of classify_quad_3p1.py: 'best if < ~2'

eccentricity_max.basis: paper section 3.1: eccentricities uniform from 0 to 0.95

outer_orbits.basis: paper section 2: 'stable' means bound and not chaotic over 100 outer orbits (a ghost run with the inner axis larger by 1e-6 au diverging by less than 1e-2 in the inner axis), not stable for a stellar lifetime

divergence_limit.basis: paper section 2: delta(t) = (a_orig - a_ghost) / a_orig above 1e-2 at any step is unstable
